version.changelog: Clearer disclosure of what is stored and where

llm.summary: The skill is coherent iOS guidance and does not show remote exfiltration, but it automatically reads and writes persistent local project, device, client, and finance notes without clear opt-in.

dimensions.detail: Darwin and xcodebuild are proportionate for native iOS work, but default access to shared business and finance stores is broader than the core platform-assistance role.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact is Markdown/JSON only, with no executable files, dependency installs, tool wrappers, startup hooks, or remote payload retrieval found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs agents to read persistent memory at session start, follow free-form Boxes entries, and write durable findings before session end; writes are announced but not generally permission-gated.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Cross-session local persistence is explicit and local, with a no-credential-storage rule, but it includes shared mutable records, deletions of rows it says it owns, free-form indexed artifacts, and a legacy data move instruction with weak pre-confirmation controls.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The iOS debugging and shipping purpose matches most content, commands, and macOS/Xcode assumptions, but the declared data scope extends into shared contacts, projects, devices, finances, and profile records beyond what many iOS tasks need.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with this skill keeping local memory about iOS apps and writing shared device, client, project, and subscription records. Review or restrict its access to ~/Clawic/data, and require explicit confirmation before any legacy-directory migration or shared-record update.
llm.findings:
[PE3] expected: The keychain references are iOS documentation and credential-handling guidance, not code that reads or steals credential files; this finding is downgraded.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The concern is supported: configPaths and memory rules include shared contacts, projects, devices, and finances, and the write policy says no permission is needed.
[RA2] expected: Local memory is part of the skill design, but the automatic cross-session read/write behavior and free-form indexed artifacts create a real review concern; repeated hits on ordinary plist/keychain/iOS text are not independently persuasive.
[T05] unexpected: The A.I.G cross-domain persistence concern is supported by SKILL.md and memory-template.md because the skill can mutate shared local business and finance records for routine iOS sessions.
[T02] unexpected: The mutable Markdown Boxes index can cause future sessions to open locally stored prose based on free-form conditions, with no strong instruction/data separation or integrity check.
[T09] expected: Moving legacy skill data is related to migration, but the instruction says to move old directories and report after the fact, which conflicts with the later confirmation guardrail for destructive or lossy changes.
